functional_requirements.title: observeOutcome core join + classification
functional_requirements.description: New lib/marketing/observer/observe-outcome.js exports observeOutcome({supabase, correlationId, mode}). It reads the venture_channel_publish_ledger row by correlation_id, then joins campaign_content on campaign_content.idempotency_key = ledger.correlation_id (both are the identical `${ventureId}:${content.id}:${platform}:<ts>` string built once in lib/marketing/publisher/index.js:39 and reused for both writes -- confirmed by direct read, no new correlation scheme). This recovers campaign_content.external_post_id and platform, which the ledger itself never stores. If the join yields no campaign_content row, or external_post_id is null (publish failed before a post existed), classify 'unmeasurable' rather than 'unknown' -- the artifact needed to ever measure this row does not exist and never will. Additionally, a literal `dry-run-*` sentinel value in campaign_content.external_post_id (emitted by both adapters in dry-run mode) must be rejected the same as a null external_post_id -- classify unmeasurable, never treat the sentinel as a real post id. campaign_content row existence alone does not prove a successful publish: the write is guarded by `if (result.success && campaignId)` in publisher/index.js, but campaign_content is ALSO written ungated by content-generator.js, so external_post_id must be checked non-null and non-sentinel, not row presence.
acceptance_criteria: observeOutcome({correlationId}) for a ledger row with a matching campaign_content row returns the platform and external_post_id recovered via the idempotency_key join
observeOutcome for a ledger row with no matching campaign_content row (or a null external_post_id) returns outcome='unmeasurable', never 'unknown' and never a guess
A campaign_content row whose external_post_id is null or a literal dry-run-* sentinel classifies unmeasurable, never shipped_clean/reverted/caused_rework

Given a deleted/invalid post URI, getPostRecord returns deletedOrErrored=true without throwing

Given a deleted tweet id (404 from the API), getTweet returns deletedOrErrored=true without throwing

functional_requirements.title: Scheduled observer step (never called from publish())
functional_requirements.description: New scripts/cron/publish-outcome-observer.mjs following this repo's established scheduled-job convention: parseArgs/main(argv,deps)/--once/--dry-run/Windows-safe gracefulExit, a matching .github/workflows/publish-outcome-observer-cron.yml (schedule: + workflow_dispatch), lib/machinery-class/armed-registration.js registerArmedMachinery, and lib/periodic-liveness/stamp-last-fired.js -- NOT the lib/eva/workers/ BaseWorker/WorkerScheduler setInterval pattern (wrong shape, does not survive process restarts). It selects ledger rows still outcome='unknown' whose created_at is inside a fixed observation window, calls observeOutcome per row, then calls recordPublishOutcome({correlationId, outcome, outcomeRef}) -- the ledger's own existing rule (autonomy-gate.js comment at :440-ish / confirmed by direct read) that recordPublishOutcome is never called from publish() itself. This scheduled step SUPERSEDES the still-owed inline recordPublishOutcome() call from the dependency SD (SD-LEO-INFRA-DEMAND-ENGINE-FAIL-001 shipped FR-3 known-incomplete: content-pipeline.js / owned-audience-content-loop.js still owe an inline call). That inline call must NOT be built -- it is the self-report anti-pattern the ledger docstring itself forbids, and building both would create two conflicting writers of the same row.
acceptance_criteria: Running the script twice against the same window is idempotent: the second run changes zero rows (keyed on correlation_id, matching the ledger's own UNIQUE(correlation_id) constraint)
The script never runs from inside publisher/index.js publish() -- verified by grep showing no import of the observer module in that file

functional_requirements.title: Mode-aware outcome recording -- net-new, not a reuse of an existing pattern
functional_requirements.description: VALIDATION (LEAD phase, sub-agent evidence 8057d0a8) measured that execution_mode is ALREADY APPLIED in the live schema (with mock_run_id; all 3 current ledger rows are execution_mode='live') -- the prior premise that this column was 'chairman-gated, not yet applied' is FALSE, and evaluateGraduation's existing 42703-fallback branch is now dead code (left in place, not removed by this SD -- out of scope to touch). The REAL gap validation found: recordPublishOutcome (lib/marketing/autonomy-gate.js:469) does a bare `.eq('correlation_id')` update with NO execution_mode filter at all -- a mock-mode outcome as written today WOULD silently overwrite a live row's outcome. This SD must ADD an execution_mode-scoped predicate to that update (match the row's own recorded execution_mode, never cross-write). evaluateGraduation (:497) is only partially mode-aware: it currently BREAKS the streak when it encounters a mock-mode row rather than filtering candidate rows by mode up front -- this SD replaces that behavior with an explicit mode filter on evaluateGraduation's SELECT (:509), so a mock-mode call only ever considers mock-mode rows and a live-mode call only ever considers live-mode rows. This is a design decision made explicitly here, not left ambiguous.
acceptance_criteria: recordPublishOutcome's UPDATE includes an execution_mode predicate matching the row being recorded (net-new code this SD -- today's implementation has none)
evaluateGraduation's candidate-row SELECT filters by execution_mode up front; it no longer relies on breaking the streak when a mismatched-mode row is encountered
A mock-mode outcome recorded via the scheduled step never changes a live-mode row's outcome or clean_streak, verified directly (TS-3, TS-6)

functional_requirements.title: Widen the outcome enum with 'unmeasurable' (no fake rework signal)
functional_requirements.description: database/migrations/<date>_venture_channel_publish_ledger_outcome_unmeasurable.sql widens venture_channel_publish_ledger's outcome CHECK constraint from ('unknown','shipped_clean','reverted','caused_rework') to add 'unmeasurable', mirroring the sibling solomon_advice_outcome_ledger precedent (database/migrations/20260828_solomon_ledger_outcome_unmeasurable.sql) exactly: purely additive DROP+re-ADD of the same named constraint, no column added, no data rewritten. No 'rework' detector is invented -- direct reads of lib/marketing/ai/metrics-ingestor.js and lib/marketing/ai/variant-outcome-derivation.js confirmed neither reads or derives per-post rework/outcome state today (metrics-ingestor normalizes inbound aggregate engagement metrics; variant-outcome-derivation derives A/B success/failure from daily_rollups impression/conversion aggregates), so caused_rework is only ever set from an explicit, already-existing rework signal if one is later wired elsewhere -- this SD does not fabricate one. This SD does not remove or alter the existing 'caused_rework' CHECK value -- it remains a valid enum member -- but no code path in this SD produces it: caused_rework is explicitly declared UNREACHABLE this increment (no rework signal exists anywhere in the codebase, confirmed independently by both LEAD's direct read and VALIDATION's re-check of metrics-ingestor.js and variant-outcome-derivation.js). A future SD wires an actual rework signal before caused_rework is ever written by this pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: The outcome CHECK constraint on venture_channel_publish_ledger accepts 'unmeasurable' after migration apply
No new heuristic 'rework' classifier is added by this SD; caused_rework is only ever produced by an existing, already-verified signal (none exists today, so it is not exercised by the new code path)

functional_requirements.title: Fixed observation window, never guess on an unreadable post
functional_requirements.description: The observation window (config constant, default matching the SD's own success_metrics fixture expectations) bounds how long the scheduled step waits before finalizing an outcome for a row. If the window elapses and the platform lookup could not be completed (network/auth error, not a 404/deleted result), the row is left 'unknown' for the next run rather than coerced to any terminal outcome -- distinct from FR-1's 'unmeasurable' (permanently unobservable) case. A literal dry-run-* sentinel or null external_post_id is rejected immediately as unmeasurable (FR-1) BEFORE the fixed-window logic ever runs -- it is not a "transient failure inside the window" case.
acceptance_criteria: A transient lookup failure inside the window leaves the row 'unknown', re-attempted on the next scheduled run
A row past the window with a confirmed-absent post is classified 'reverted', never left 'unknown' forever

functional_requirements.title: Live-outcome proof is out of scope this increment; deliver and prove the mechanism in mock mode only
functional_requirements.description: VALIDATION (LEAD phase) measured that AltifyAI -- the only venture this SD's spine names as its subject -- has ZERO rows across venture_channel_secrets, channel_budgets, venture_channel_publish_ledger, venture_channel_autonomy, and venture_demand_verdicts, AND is blocked by a recorded chairman ruling (ventures.metadata.outreach_ruling = BLOCKED, scope 'any outbound contact with a real human being', blocked_until 'S24 Launch Readiness PASS AND S25 Go Live PASS', with the 23->24 transition currently PARKED). Provisioning AltifyAI's channels and clearing that gate are both explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this SD. As originally scoped, the SD's own success criteria and smoke-test step ('observe one AltifyAI post published in a prior run') had NO SUBJECT and could never be satisfied without either violating the outreach ruling's intent or silently assuming an interpretation of its scope that only the chairman can rule on. Per the chairman's own standing policy (2026-09-12: no real-customer outreach before go-live stage; mock first; Solomon plans the go-live sequencing), this SD resolves the question conservatively WITHOUT needing to escalate the interpretation: it proves the full mechanism (join, adapter lookups, mode-scoped recordPublishOutcome, evaluateGraduation invocation) end-to-end against a MOCK-mode fixture/test post it creates itself, and does not attempt to observe or act on any real AltifyAI (or other venture's) live post. A live-post-based proof remains a named, explicit external dependency on (a) AltifyAI provisioning and (b) the S24/S25 gate clearing -- tracked, not silently assumed, and not delivered by this SD.
acceptance_criteria: evaluateGraduation runs at least once from a recorded MOCK-mode outcome produced by this SD's new scheduled path (replacing the SD-spine's original live-outcome criterion, which had no reachable subject)

No code path in this SD reads, writes, or otherwise acts on a real AltifyAI post or any other real, unprovisioned venture -- verified by the mock-mode fixture being self-contained test data, never a live query result
The live-outcome proof gap (AltifyAI provisioning + S24/S25 clearing) is recorded as a named external dependency in integration_operationalization, not silently dropped or assumed resolved

The five other reached_how families are named explicitly as out-of-scope in integration_operationalization.dependencies, not omitted

system_architecture.summary: A new read-only observer module joins the publish ledger to campaign_content to recover real post ids, looks posts up via two new adapter methods, and feeds the existing (currently unreachable) mode-aware graduation path through a scheduled job -- never through publish() itself. recordPublishOutcome/evaluateGraduation are modified (not reused as-is) to add the execution_mode scoping validation found missing.
